assessment.summary: TREM2 is a well-characterized immunoreceptor with strong structural evidence (15 PDB entries at up to 1.47Å resolution, 11 with bound ligands) and robust disease validation in Alzheimer's disease and neurodegeneration. Despite zero ChEMBL IC50 entries, a 2026 first-in-human oral small-molecule agonist (VG-3927/SAR448851) confirms that the target is chemically tractable, representing a significant data lag in ChEMBL. Overall druggability is medium-to-high, tempered by the absence of approved drugs and the biological complexity of context-dependent TREM2 signalling.
evidence_gaps: ChEMBL has zero IC50 entries despite clinical-stage small molecules existing — significant database lag
No approved drugs for TREM2 to date
Selectivity profile against TREM1 and other TREM family members not captured in available data
Intracellular and transmembrane domain structural coverage is limited; AlphaFold pLDDT only moderate (76.8 mean)
Context-dependent biology (pro-inflammatory in cancer vs. neuroprotective in neurodegeneration) complicates therapeutic strategy
Binding mode and SAR for the clinical-stage agonist VG-3927/SAR448851 not yet publicly available
In vivo pharmacodynamic and target engagement data for small-molecule agonists not yet in public domain
